mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25 percentage points for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth falls below -2% for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when this trigger is met (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE exceeds 6% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which depresses earnings for industrial firms and drags the S&P 500 lower over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant negative S&P 500 60-day returns observed when INDPRO declines by > 0.5% for four months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.3% in the same month signals a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with weakening inflation, which historically precedes equity market corrections over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls by > 0.3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls by > 0.3% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in housing starts (HOUST) and personal savings (RSAFS) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a demand expansion driven by both increased investment and higher household savings, which supports higher equity valuations over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both exceed 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both HOUST and RSAFS exceed their 12-month moving averages in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of at least 50,000 for six consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 50,000 for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS increases by at least 50,000 for six consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) above 4% for two consecutive quarters indicates a strong economic expansion, which elevates earnings expectations and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when annualized GDPC1 exceeds 4% for two consecutive quarters.
